finding.expected: Bind local-chat-wake eligibility to the exact successful terminal admission outputs/status rather than success of the entire mixed admit-and-notify job, while preserving fail-closed behavior when admission itself is absent/failed/ambiguous. Keep terminal attention permissions at contents:read plus issues:write, preserve the existing Issue/artifact path as independent observability, and add deterministic regressions proving post-admission notification/artifact failure cannot suppress an admitted local wake while admission failure cannot trigger one.
finding.issue: The new local-chat wake job is gated on needs.admit-and-notify.result == 'success'. That job contains canonical terminal admission plus unrelated downstream Issue notification and wake-source artifact/export steps. If exact terminal admission succeeds but Issue creation, selector writing, or artifact export fails afterward, the job result is failure and the local-chat wake is skipped. TASK-262 r2 requires the production wake wiring to originate after successful canonical terminal-attention admission; unrelated legacy/observability transport failure must not suppress an otherwise admitted local wake.

original_constraints: Production transport wiring must originate only after successful canonical terminal-attention admission and hand off to the repository-owned local-chat-wake workflow without workflow_run, Work, polling, schedules, or Issue re-triggering.

Terminal attention must retain its pre-H4A2 top-level permission set of contents:read plus issues:write. H4A2 must not require actions:write on the terminal-attention workflow; use a bounded reusable-workflow/job handoff for the local wake path.
Automatic production delivery remains controlled by an explicit Human-operated noncanonical enable gate and must be disabled or no-op when that gate is absent or false.
No H4A2 code path may mutate canonical AIOS refs/artifacts, allocate lifecycle identities, infer next_action, select semantic flow/correction, or advance roadmap state.
